Structured triangular mesh of a rectangle

Source: R/mesh.R
pde_mesh_rectangle.Rd

Splits the rectangle into nx by ny cells and each cell into two triangles.

Usage

pde_mesh_rectangle(
  x = c(0, 1),
  y = c(0, 1),
  nx = 8,
  ny = nx,
  pattern = c("right", "left", "alternating")
)

Arguments

x, y

Endpoints of the rectangle in each direction.

nx, ny

Number of cells in each direction.

pattern

Diagonal pattern: "right" (diagonals from lower left to upper right), "left" (lower right to upper left) or "alternating" (the diagonal direction alternates from cell to cell).

Value

A pde_mesh with boundary markers "bottom", "right", "top" and "left". Corner nodes belong to both adjacent sides.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 4, ny = 4)
summary(mesh)
#> Triangular mesh summary
#>   nodes 25  elements 32  edges 56  boundary edges 16 
#>   total area         1 
#>   edge length: min  0.25  max 0.3536 
#>   angles (deg): min    45  max    90 
#>   shape ratio 2r/R: min 0.8284  median 0.8284  max 0.8284 
#>   boundary edges by marker:
#>     bottom: 4
#>     left: 4
#>     right: 4
#>     top: 4
